edit.description: the one place a closed stdout is answered, ahead of every verb's writes
the closed-pipe cases for an observational verb

summary: a reader that closes the pipe mid-listing ends a verb's writes quietly, keeping the exit code the verb would have had
acceptance: `flume status | head -1` exits 0 with no stack trace and no unhandled stdout error, and every verb that writes a listing keeps the exit code it would have had when its reader goes away; the answer is at the CLI's own output point, never per verb
tests: status exits 0 when its reader closes the pipe before the listing ends
a verb whose reader closed the pipe prints no unhandled-error trace
a closed stdout leaves a refusing verb's own exit code intact
notes: Measured 2026-10-07 on Node 24.21.0: `pnpm flume status | head -2` died with `Error: write EPIPE` out of `console.log` in `statusVerb`. The cited section gives status no failure mode outside an unreadable file it must read, so a crash here prints an observation as its opposite. Every stdout-writing verb shares the door; `src/cliStatus.ts` is only where it was seen.
